title: Shown
description:
One artifact in full, as `show` shows it: what it is, where it is, what
its front matter declares that `show` prints, and the body after it.

allowed_tools.description: A skill's `allowed-tools`, when it narrows them.

body.description: What follows the front matter, as the file has it now.

compatibility.description: A skill's `compatibility`, when written as the string it should be.

description.description:
What it says it is for: always for a skill, and for a rule only when
its front matter says.

expressibility.description:
What each agent cannot be given of an MCP server's definition, every
agent's in report order ([`crate::mcp::McpDefinition::expressibility`]):
none for a skill or a rule, which every agent reads as it is.

file.description: The file it is read from: a skill's `SKILL.md`, or the rule itself.

license.description: A skill's `license`, when it names one.

metadata.description:
Each `metadata` entry of a skill that maps a string to a string, in
the order written: the rest are `validate`'s to report. None for a
rule, which has no `metadata`.

path.description:
The directory a skill is, or the file a rule is: its first copy's,
the one `show` reads.

paths.description: The files a rule is about, as glob patterns, when it says.

project.description:
The root of what holds it: its project, or the workspace for the
workspace's own.

summary.description: The one line a listing shows; none when there is nothing to show.

Agent.description: A coding agent, by the name `--agents` and a project's settings take.

Expressibility.description:
What one agent cannot be given of a definition, as `show` says it: the
agent, by the word a command line takes for it, then what refuses it
the definition and what it is given the definition without, each by
its code and in its words.

Both lists empty, and the agent is given the definition whole; one
thing refused, and it is given none of it, whatever else is dropped.

dropped.description:
What its entry is written without, in the order the definition
holds it.

refused.description:
What it cannot be given at all, in the order the definition holds
it: any one of them, and its renderer writes it no entry.

Kind.description: A kind of artifact, by the word a command line takes for it.

Said.description:
An error as a serialized type holds one: its code, for a front end to act
on, and its message, for whoever reads it.

Built where the type is serialized, or kept in what a front end reads
(the workspace's snapshot), in place of the error, since an error
holds what JSON has no shape for (an `io::Error`, a parser's own), and
only these two are meant to leave core. Its fields are public for a
front end that reads the snapshot as Rust rather than as JSON, the TUI.

message.description:
Written through [`redacted`](crate::url::redacted), as every URL
is: an error can quote one, a source's among them, and what built
the error is no promise that it carries no credential.
